relevance_note: A retrospective cohort of 260 patients with inherited metabolic diseases that singles out one patient with LCAT deficiency who had diabetes: "The primary diagnosis of one of these two patients was lecithin-cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) deficiency".
method_note: Read by hand; no script transcription. One in-scope person: the patient whose primary diagnosis was LCAT deficiency, labelled 'unnamed person 1' (no paper label; not a case report). The only individual-level fact is diabetes mellitus; no sex, age, variant, genetic testing or lipid/renal/ocular findings are given, so no variant row was created (the paper ties no LCAT variant to the person) and all 20 checklist items are not reported. Excluded rows come from the named-group statement 'None of the patients with IMD had pubertal or GH disorders nor disorders related to thyroid, mineralocorticoid hormones, or bone disorders.' Glucocorticoid deficiency was not marked excluded because the paper says it was assessed only in 248 of 260 patients and does not say whether this patient was among them. Growth retardation (27 of 258) is not attributed by person. The paper calls the diagnosis 'LCAT deficiency' without saying familial or how it was diagnosed. Table 1 is listed but its content is missing from the converted text. Minor inconsistency: the paper gives 2 of 260 as '0.07%'.
